speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your follow-up appointment. Please describe in detail how you would characterize the "shooting" ear pain, including its duration, frequency, and what specifically makes it worse when wearing earrings. Also, tell me exactly what occurred during your recent tympanoplasty surgery.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuralgia of the Great Auricular Nerve. The clinical picture of shooting ear pain triggered by eating (jaw movement) and specific tenderness when wearing earrings (pressure on the nerve's course over the mastoid) following a recent tympanoplasty is classic for this complication. While a trial of oral analgesics and avoiding pressure on the ear may be suggested, no further diagnostic tests are required to confirm this diagnosis based on your detailed history.
